by_quarantine_region.justification: CIC describes Infiltration as two stages — "First level: Dropbox download in a windows machine. Second Level: Nmap and portscan" — and Table 2 publishes only the first. It names the infected host in the Victim column (172.31.69.24 on 28-02, 172.31.69.13 on 01-03), but never the scan targets and never a separate window for the second stage. The internal scan is therefore unlabellable from the schedule: we cannot say which flows it produced, so every one of them falls to benign by the closed-world assumption. That default is not neutral here. The attack rules match 8 flows across roughly 4.5 scheduled hours, while these windows carry on the order of 175,000 unmatched flows per 10-minute bucket — a benign class certified by nothing but the absence of a published target list. The 8 matched flows are no better founded than the unmatched ones: none of them completed a connection (conn_state OTH 50% / S1 37.5% / RSTR 12.5%) and the longest runs 13,254.7 s against a 5,820 s window, a 2.28x overrun, so they are mid-stream traffic caught by a time window rather than an observed attack (B11). They sit inside these regions and are quarantined with everything else; `infiltration` therefore carries no adjudicable evidence in this dataset and must not be evaluated as a class (B10). DistriNet derives the two phases as running to 18:39 and 19:38, far past CIC's published 14:40 and 15:37, so even as declared these regions UNDER-cover the phase (A3). They are drawn at the published times because those are what the source states; the DistriNet finding is why the region cannot be read as an upper bound on the contamination. Widening them, or replacing them with real second-stage attack rules, is DEFERRED until sch.window_sweep has measured where this traffic actually stops in our own lake: the DistriNet end times are a third party's derivation and are recorded as the hypothesis that sweep should test, never as a transcribed fact. Scoped to the hosts CIC does name, so the rest of each day — which the schedule describes normally — stays adjudicated. These regions coincide with the four scheduled Infiltration windows by construction, so qtn.overlap_with_attack reports them: we are declining to adjudicate a span the schedule claims. That contradiction is real and this is its answer — the schedule's claim here amounts to 8 unfinished flows and accounts for none of the rest.
